A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it is a study on motherhood, care work and inequality, from the perspective of the women who perform it.

we have tried to describe the experiences of maternity in two groups of women: one of them, women domestic workers, who have migrated to Buenos Aires from different countries of Latin America, and the other one, women who employ them.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the care of the child, as well as the care of the mother, is a complex process, in which different social and economic factors play an important role, which in turn, are linked to the social and cultural context in which they are developed.
the reproduction of social inequality in the area of childcare is a process that involves a complex interweaving of social, cultural, and economic factors.

the reproduction of the stratification is a process that is not only related to the economic and social conditions of the women, but it is also a result of the different ways of organizing care and attention, as well as the different ways of conceiving motherhood, that is to say, the different ways of being a mother.
